title: a LevelSequence with tracks and keyframes
proves: author a sequence with bindings, tracks and keys, read it back, place it in the level and play it

steps.label: primitive puerts_sequence_render is NOT usable
steps.detail: NEW: not registered, and no legacy tool in the inventory covers it either
steps.why: render a LevelSequence to image frames or a video so the result of a cinematic prompt can be looked at. puerts_viewport_screenshot captures one editor viewport frame and cannot follow a sequence's camera cuts

steps.label: 1. build the intro sequence with two bound tracks and five keys
2. read the sequence back and count the keys that actually landed
3. place a LevelSequenceActor that points at it
4. render the three seconds so the result can be looked at
5. what this slice is really reporting
steps.detail: cinematics is the only one of the seven domains with no owner and no partial support. Four primitives are missing and three of them are unowned. The nearest existing code, title_sequence_bind, writes a JSON scaffold and its own runtime_note says a dedicated Sequencer bridge tool is required.

missing_primitives.why: render a LevelSequence to image frames or a video so the result of a cinematic prompt can be looked at. puerts_viewport_screenshot captures one editor viewport frame and cannot follow a sequence's camera cuts

proposed_schema.note: UE4.27 ships Movie Render Queue as a plugin; the fallback is the older FSequencerRenderer / automated level sequence capture path. Which one is available is a project-settings question, so the tool must report which it used.
